## Context

Gerrit review of change 1536 confirmed the new locked commit-and-push entrypoint safely fails
closed when local lock-artifact exclusion cannot be installed, and that the pre-lock update may
append harmless duplicate exclude lines under concurrent first use. Preserve the shipped
compatibility contract while tightening the local metadata update and its direct failure
oracles.

## Current state (verified against origin/main cc69cc1179)

`_ignore_lock_artifacts` (src/rebar/_store/push.py:606-629) resolves `info/exclude`, reads it,
computes the missing patterns, and appends them with a buffered `open(..., "a")` that can issue
TWO writes (a leading newline, then the patterns). It is called at push.py:651, BEFORE the write
lock is taken — deliberately, since the exclusion must exist before anything can stage — so two
first-time callers genuinely race here.

Two racing buffered appends can interleave at the byte level and tear a pattern into a corrupt
half-line (e.g. `.ticket-write.lo`), which would silently stop excluding the lock artifact. That
is the real hazard; a duplicated WHOLE line is not.

Test coverage gaps in tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py (331 lines): the
existing tests cover `git add` / `git commit` failure (line 190), lock failure (228), the
recovery guard (156), push-only (259) and the CLI (277). Nothing directly covers the
exclusion-write failure gate (push.py:651-655), the `git status` failure gate (push.py:673-678),
or proves that lock artifacts stay out of a real commit.

## Plan

1. push.py `_ignore_lock_artifacts`: hoist the pattern tuple to a module constant and replace the
   buffered two-write append with a SINGLE `os.write` to an `O_WRONLY|O_APPEND` descriptor. POSIX
   applies that one write at end-of-file atomically, so a racing pair can no longer tear a
   pattern. Document in the docstring that a duplicated whole line remains possible and is the
   deliberate disposition — git applies a repeated exclude pattern identically, so the file stays
   semantically idempotent, and removing the duplicate would require a lock this function must
   not take (it runs before the write lock and stays outside the recovery guard, both unchanged).
   Do not change the read-failure disposition (`OSError` still returns False / fails closed).
   Scope note: single-write `O_APPEND` atomicity is a POSIX guarantee, which matches this
   project's declared support surface — pyproject.toml classifies it `Operating System :: POSIX`
   and `MacOS :: MacOS X` (no Windows classifier) and every CI job runs on `ubuntu-latest`. The
   docstring states that scope rather than implying a universal guarantee.
2. Tests, added to the held-out file:
   - exclusion-write failure, strict and default: force `_ignore_lock_artifacts` to fail and
     assert strict raises `PushDeliveryError` with reason `stage-failed` while default logs a
     warning and returns; the dirty content is retained and a clean retry commits and delivers.
   - `git status` failure, strict and default: same split, same retained-content + clean-retry
     oracle, reaching the push.py:673-678 branch specifically.
   - real legacy-tracker commit: with both lock artifacts present on disk, commit and assert via
     `git ls-tree -r` that neither `.ticket-write.lock` nor anything under `.ticket-write.lock.d/`
     entered the committed tree, and that a clean retry succeeds.
   - concurrent first use: run the exclude update from several workers against one fresh tracker
     and assert every line of `info/exclude` is a whole, intact pattern (no torn line) and both
     patterns are present.
3. Keep push.py within the 800-line module-size gate — it is at 789 today, so the change must be
   close to net-neutral.

## Testing

- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit/test_commit_and_push_tickets_branch_heldout.py -q` (the held-out commit-and-push suite).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" python -m pytest tests/unit -k "push" -q` (the push-only compatibility suites).
- `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`.
- `awk 'END{print NR}' src/rebar/_store/push.py` stays at or below the 800 in `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] AC1 — Concurrent first use cannot corrupt local exclude metadata on the supported POSIX platforms; duplicate-line disposition is documented or eliminated. Proved by the concurrent-first-use test asserting no torn line.
- [x] AC2 — Strict and default exclusion/status failures are directly covered with observable typed-error or warning/return outcomes. Proved by the four new failure tests (`stage-failed` reason vs caplog warning + return).
- [x] AC3 — A real legacy tracker commit proves lock artifacts are absent from the resulting commit and a clean retry succeeds. Proved by the `git ls-tree -r` oracle over the committed tree.
- [x] AC4 — Existing push-only and commit-and-push compatibility suites remain green, checked by the pytest commands above; `make lint` and `make typecheck` pass and push.py stays within the module-size gate.
